properties.name: Roxbury
properties.title: Roxbury
properties.text:
Studio: $1,300–$1,500/mo · 1BR: $1,600–$2,000/mo · 2BR: $2,450–$2,850/mo
Boston's historic African-American heart, rich in culture and community organizations.
Most affordable inner-city neighborhood with significant development underway.

properties.name: Dorchester
properties.title: Dorchester
properties.text:
Studio: $1,350–$1,550/mo · 1BR: $1,700–$2,150/mo · 2BR: $2,550–$3,000/mo
Boston's largest and most diverse neighborhood with deep community roots.
Affordable rents, improving transit, and ongoing investment make it a rising area.

properties.name: Mission Hill
properties.title: Mission Hill
properties.text:
Studio: $1,500–$1,700/mo · 1BR: $1,900–$2,350/mo · 2BR: $2,850–$3,300/mo
Student and working-class neighborhood close to Northeastern and Harvard Medical.
Affordable by Boston standards with a tight-knit community feel.

properties.name: Allston
properties.title: Allston
properties.text:
Studio: $1,500–$1,700/mo · 1BR: $1,900–$2,350/mo · 2BR: $2,850–$3,300/mo
The city's music and dive-bar capital, beloved by students and young creatives.
Affordable rents and infamous August move-out chaos define the neighborhood.

properties.name: East Boston
properties.title: East Boston
properties.text:
Studio: $1,600–$1,800/mo · 1BR: $2,000–$2,450/mo · 2BR: $2,950–$3,500/mo
Rapidly gentrifying waterfront neighborhood with a vibrant Latino community.
Stunning harbor views, direct Blue Line to downtown, and rising rents.

properties.name: The Port
properties.title: The Port
properties.text:
Studio: $1,650–$1,900/mo · 1BR: $2,050–$2,600/mo · 2BR: $3,100–$3,650/mo
One of Cambridge's most diverse and affordable neighborhoods near Central Square.
Strong community identity and a grassroots arts scene.

properties.name: Jamaica Plain
properties.title: Jamaica Plain
properties.text:
Studio: $1,750–$1,950/mo · 1BR: $2,150–$2,700/mo · 2BR: $3,250–$3,800/mo
Diverse, artsy, and beloved by families and creatives alike.
Jamaica Pond, independent restaurants, and good Orange Line access.

properties.name: Wellington-Harrington
properties.title: Wellington-Harrington
properties.text:
Studio: $1,750–$1,950/mo · 1BR: $2,150–$2,700/mo · 2BR: $3,250–$3,800/mo
Working-class Cambridge neighborhood with a growing creative community.
More affordable than most of Cambridge with improving amenities.

properties.name: Neighborhood Nine
properties.title: Neighborhood Nine
properties.text:
Studio: $1,800–$2,050/mo · 1BR: $2,250–$2,800/mo · 2BR: $3,400–$3,950/mo
Boston-area neighborhood with a mix of residential and commercial uses.
Convenient to downtown with strong transit connections.

properties.name: North Cambridge
properties.title: North Cambridge
properties.text:
Studio: $1,800–$2,050/mo · 1BR: $2,250–$2,800/mo · 2BR: $3,400–$3,950/mo
Boston-area neighborhood with a mix of residential and commercial uses.
Convenient to downtown with strong transit connections.

properties.name: West Cambridge
properties.title: West Cambridge
properties.text:
Studio: $1,800–$2,050/mo · 1BR: $2,250–$2,800/mo · 2BR: $3,400–$3,950/mo
Boston-area neighborhood with a mix of residential and commercial uses.
Convenient to downtown with strong transit connections.

properties.name: Baldwin
properties.title: Baldwin
properties.text:
Studio: $1,800–$2,050/mo · 1BR: $2,250–$2,800/mo · 2BR: $3,400–$3,950/mo
Small Cambridge neighborhood with a mix of housing types.
Relatively affordable with good access to transit and local amenities.

properties.name: MIT
properties.title: MIT
properties.text:
Studio: $1,800–$2,050/mo · 1BR: $2,250–$2,800/mo · 2BR: $3,400–$3,950/mo
Boston-area neighborhood with a mix of residential and commercial uses.
Convenient to downtown with strong transit connections.

properties.name: Chinatown
properties.title: Chinatown
properties.text:
Studio: $1,850–$2,150/mo · 1BR: $2,350–$2,900/mo · 2BR: $3,500–$4,100/mo
Dense urban neighborhood — the only surviving Chinatown in New England.
Authentic cuisine, strong community ties, and proximity to Tufts Medical.

properties.name: Cambridgeport
properties.title: Cambridgeport
properties.text:
Studio: $1,850–$2,150/mo · 1BR: $2,350–$2,900/mo · 2BR: $3,500–$4,100/mo
Dense residential neighborhood between MIT and Central Square.
Affordable for Cambridge, with a diverse mix of students, families, and professionals.

properties.name: Longwood
properties.title: Longwood
properties.text:
Studio: $1,950–$2,200/mo · 1BR: $2,450–$3,000/mo · 2BR: $3,650–$4,250/mo
Boston's Medical District, surrounded by world-class hospitals.
Stable, in-demand rental market driven by healthcare workers and residents.

properties.name: Fenway
properties.title: Fenway
properties.text:
Studio: $2,000–$2,300/mo · 1BR: $2,500–$3,150/mo · 2BR: $3,800–$4,400/mo
Student-heavy neighborhood anchored by Fenway Park and several universities.
Active nightlife and improving infrastructure attract a young professional crowd.

properties.name: West End
properties.title: West End
properties.text:
Studio: $2,000–$2,300/mo · 1BR: $2,500–$3,150/mo · 2BR: $3,800–$4,400/mo
Once a dense immigrant neighborhood, now high-rises near MGH.
Convenient to downtown and Beacon Hill; limited street-level charm.

properties.name: Riverside
properties.title: Riverside
properties.text:
Studio: $2,000–$2,300/mo · 1BR: $2,500–$3,150/mo · 2BR: $3,800–$4,400/mo
Quiet Cambridge neighborhood along the Charles River.
Popular with MIT-affiliated residents and families seeking green space.

properties.name: Mid-Cambridge
properties.title: Mid-Cambridge
properties.text:
Studio: $2,150–$2,450/mo · 1BR: $2,700–$3,350/mo · 2BR: $4,050–$4,750/mo
Central Cambridge residential neighborhood between Harvard and Inman Square.
Quiet tree-lined streets popular with academics and long-term residents.

properties.name: Bay Village
properties.title: Bay Village
properties.text:
Studio: $2,250–$2,550/mo · 1BR: $2,800–$3,450/mo · 2BR: $4,200–$4,900/mo
Boston's smallest neighborhood — a quiet enclave off the Theatre District.
Federal-style rowhouses on narrow, tree-lined streets.

properties.name: North End
properties.title: North End
properties.text:
Studio: $2,250–$2,550/mo · 1BR: $2,800–$3,450/mo · 2BR: $4,200–$4,900/mo
Boston's oldest neighborhood, shaped by its Italian-American heritage.
Cobblestone streets, world-class restaurants, and stunning harbor views.

properties.name: Charlestown
properties.title: Charlestown
properties.text:
Studio: $2,300–$2,600/mo · 1BR: $2,900–$3,600/mo · 2BR: $4,300–$5,050/mo
Historic waterfront neighborhood anchored by the Bunker Hill Monument.
Mix of townhouses and Navy Yard condos with sweeping harbor views.

properties.name: South Boston
properties.title: South Boston
properties.text:
Studio: $2,300–$2,600/mo · 1BR: $2,900–$3,600/mo · 2BR: $4,300–$5,050/mo
From working-class 'Southie' roots to sought-after luxury condos.
Beaches, craft breweries, and rents that have doubled in a decade.

properties.name: East Cambridge
properties.title: East Cambridge
properties.text:
Studio: $2,300–$2,600/mo · 1BR: $2,900–$3,600/mo · 2BR: $4,300–$5,050/mo
Tech and biotech workers fill this Kendall Square–adjacent neighborhood.
Proximity to MIT and top-tier research labs drives relentless demand.

properties.name: Government Center/Faneuil Hall
properties.title: Government Center/Faneuil Hall
properties.text:
Studio: $2,450–$2,800/mo · 1BR: $3,050–$3,800/mo · 2BR: $4,600–$5,350/mo
Busy civic hub anchored by Faneuil Hall Marketplace and City Hall.
Limited residential stock keeps vacancy near zero year-round.

properties.name: Downtown
properties.title: Downtown
properties.text:
Studio: $2,600–$2,950/mo · 1BR: $3,250–$4,050/mo · 2BR: $4,850–$5,700/mo
Boston's commercial core, walkable to everything.
Luxury high-rises and converted offices; quieter than expected on weekends.

properties.name: South End
properties.title: South End
properties.text:
Studio: $2,650–$3,050/mo · 1BR: $3,350–$4,150/mo · 2BR: $5,000–$5,850/mo
Victorian rowhouses, a thriving restaurant scene, and a vibrant arts community.
Boston's most LGBTQ-friendly neighborhood with a dynamic cultural mix.

properties.name: Leather District
properties.title: Leather District
properties.text:
Studio: $2,750–$3,100/mo · 1BR: $3,400–$4,250/mo · 2BR: $5,150–$6,000/mo
Converted warehouse lofts near South Station, popular with tech and design workers.
Small but highly sought-after with authentic urban industrial character.

properties.name: Beacon Hill
properties.title: Beacon Hill
properties.text:
Studio: $2,800–$3,200/mo · 1BR: $3,500–$4,350/mo · 2BR: $5,250–$6,150/mo
Gas-lit streets, Federal rowhouses, and the State House dome.
One of the most prestigious and historically preserved corners of Boston.

properties.name: Back Bay
properties.title: Back Bay
properties.text:
Studio: $3,000–$3,450/mo · 1BR: $3,800–$4,700/mo · 2BR: $5,650–$6,650/mo
Boston's most iconic address — Victorian brownstones on Commonwealth Ave.
Newbury St boutiques and the Esplanade make it endlessly desirable.

properties.name: Seaport
properties.title: Seaport
properties.text:
Studio: $3,450–$3,950/mo · 1BR: $4,300–$5,400/mo · 2BR: $6,500–$7,600/mo
Boston's newest luxury district, built on the innovation economy.
Modern towers and waterfront dining with the highest rents in the city.
